items.title: 9.8 Solubility product (for slightly soluble ionic compounds)

source_refs.note: Topic 9.8 (Solubility Product) with Table 9.5, printed pages 201-202. Table cell typos are marked; the print's 'SO4 2- and SO4 2-' for the dissolved ions is read as Pb2+ and SO4 2-.

blocks.text: When a soluble ionic compound such as NaCl is dissolved in water it dissociates completely into ions, but for slightly soluble salts the dissociation is not complete at equilibrium. When PbSO4 is shaken with water, the solution contains Pb2+, SO4 2- and undissociated PbSO4, so an equilibrium exists between the solid solute and the dissolved ions. Lead sulphate is a well-known sparingly soluble compound and dissociates to a very small extent, like PbCl2: PbSO4(s) gives Pb2+(aq) + SO4 2-(aq), with Kc = [Pb2+][SO4 2-] / [PbSO4]. Being sparingly soluble, the concentration of PbSO4 remains almost constant and is taken to the left with Kc: Kc [PbSO4] = [Pb2+][SO4 2-], and with Kc [PbSO4] = Ksp, Ksp = [Pb2+][SO4 2-] = 1.6 x 10^-8 at 25 degrees C.

blocks.title: Solubility product
blocks.text: Ksp, the solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt, is the product of the molar solubilities of its ions at equilibrium, each concentration raised to an exponent equal to the coefficient in the balanced equation. For PbCl2, Ksp = [Pb2+][Cl-]^2. Ksp is usually a very small quantity at room temperature, its value depends on temperature, and it is a measure of the dissociation of the sparingly soluble salt.

blocks.caption: Ksp values of some slightly soluble ionic compounds (Table 9.5)

blocks.prompt: Write the Ksp expressions for Ag2CrO4, Al(OH)3 and Fe2S3, and say why the solid does not appear in them.
blocks.explanation: Ag2CrO4: Ksp = [Ag+]^2 [CrO4 2-]; Al(OH)3: Ksp = [Al3+][OH-]^3; Fe2S3: Ksp = [Fe3+]^2 [S2-]^3. The undissolved solid is in large excess and its concentration is constant, so it is multiplied into Kc to give Ksp, exactly as water was absorbed into Kw.

items: Sparingly soluble salt in water: solid in equilibrium with its ions; Ksp = Kc [solid] = product of ion concentrations raised to their coefficients (PbSO4 1.6 x 10^-8; PbCl2 = [Pb2+][Cl-]^2); very small, temperature dependent, a measure of dissociation.
Table 9.5 ranges from MgCO3 3.5 x 10^-8 and PbSO4 1.6 x 10^-8 down to Fe2S3 1.4 x 10^-85.
